alt: Graph of y = x^2 - 4x from x = 0 to x = 4: the shaded region lies below the x-axis, so the integral is negative (-32/3) but the area enclosed is 32/3 square units.
caption: Figure: the region below the axis gives a negative integral; its area is 32/3

alt: The line y = 2x + 3 lies above the curve y = x^2 between their intersection points (-1, 1) and (3, 9); the shaded region between them has area 32/3 square units, found by integrating (2x + 3 - x^2) from -1 to 3.
caption: Figure: the area between a line and a curve is the integral of top minus bottom

alt: Graph of y = x^2 with P(3, 9): the chord to Q(4, 16) has gradient 7, the chord to the point with x = 3.1 has gradient 6.1, and as Q moves towards P the chords approach the tangent at P, whose gradient is 6.
caption: Figure: chord gradients 7, 6.1, ... close in on the tangent gradient 6 at P

alt: Circle with centre (3, -2) and radius 5, equation (x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 25; the point (7, 1) is at distance 5 from the centre (a 3-4-5 triangle) and (-2, -2) lies on the circle too.
caption: Figure: the circle (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 25

alt: Circle (x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 25 with centre C(2, -3) and the tangent 3x + 4y - 19 = 0 touching it at P(5, 1); the tangent is perpendicular to the radius CP, which has gradient 4/3 while the tangent has gradient -3/4.
caption: Figure: the tangent at P is perpendicular to the radius CP

alt: Graph of y = 2x^2 - 4x - 6 = 2(x - 1)^2 - 8: a U-shaped curve with minimum point (1, -8), x-intercepts (-1, 0) and (3, 0), y-intercept (0, -6), symmetrical about the dashed line x = 1.
caption: Figure: y = 2(x − 1)² − 8 with its vertex, intercepts and line of symmetry

alt: Graph of y = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3): the cubic rises from the bottom left, crosses the x-axis at -2, 1 and 3 and the y-axis at (0, 6), and ends at the top right; it is positive between -2 and 1 and beyond 3.
caption: Figure: y = (x + 2)(x − 1)(x − 3) crosses the x-axis at −2, 1 and 3

alt: The line y = 2x - 2 touches the curve y = x^2 - 4x + 7 at exactly one point, (3, 4): equal roots (discriminant 0) means the line is a tangent.
caption: Figure: with c = −2 the line y = 2x + c just touches the curve at (3, 4)

alt: Graph of f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 10 for 0 to 5: it falls from (0, 10) to the minimum (3, 1) and rises to (5, 5), so the range is 1 to 10; the highest value comes from the end point x = 0, not from x = 5.
caption: Figure: for 0 ≤ x ≤ 5 the range of f is 1 ≤ f(x) ≤ 10

alt: Graphs of y = 2^x (through (0, 1), approaching the x-axis on the left) and y = log base 2 of x (through (1, 0), approaching the y-axis downwards); they are reflections of each other in the dashed line y = x.
caption: Figure: y = 2ˣ and y = log₂ x are mirror images in y = x

alt: Graphs of f(x) = (x - 1)^2 + 4 for x at least 1 (vertex at (1, 4)) and its inverse f^-1(x) = 1 + square root of (x - 4) (starting at (4, 1)); the two curves are mirror images in the dashed line y = x.
caption: Figure: f and its inverse are reflections in the line y = x

alt: Straight-line graph of lg y against lg x through (0.2, 1.1) and (0.8, 2.6): the gradient 1.5 divided by 0.6 is 2.5, which is the power n, and the intercept on the vertical axis is 0.6, which is lg A.
caption: Figure: for y = Axⁿ the line of lg y against lg x has gradient n and intercept lg A

alt: Graph of y = |2cos x + 1| for 0 to 360 degrees: starts at 3, falls to a cusp at 120 degrees, rises to 1 at 180 degrees (the reflected minimum), falls to a cusp at 240 degrees and rises back to 3 at 360 degrees.
caption: Figure: y = |2cos x + 1| with cusps at 120° and 240°

alt: Graph of y = |x^2 - 2x - 8|: cusps at (-2, 0) and (4, 0), the reflected arch peaking at (1, 9) and crossing the y-axis at (0, 8). The line y = 5 meets it four times, y = 9 three times, y = 12 twice.
caption: Figure: y = |x² − 2x − 8| and the lines y = 5, 9 and 12

alt: Graph of y = x^2 - x - 12 crossing the x-axis at -3 and 4; the part of the curve below the axis, marked in red on the axis, lies between the roots, so x^2 - x - 12 < 0 for -3 < x < 4.
caption: Figure: the curve is below the x-axis between its roots, so x² − x − 12 < 0 there

alt: Sector OAB of radius 8 cm and angle 1.2 radians: the arc length is 8 times 1.2 = 9.6 cm, the area is half of 8 squared times 1.2 = 38.4 square centimetres, and the perimeter is 8 + 8 + 9.6 = 25.6 cm.
caption: Figure: a sector of radius 8 cm and angle 1.2 radians

alt: Sector OAB with radius 10 cm and angle 1.4 radians: the chord AB is 12.9 cm, the arc is 14 cm, and the shaded minor segment between the chord and the arc has area 20.7 square centimetres (sector area minus triangle area).
caption: Figure: the minor segment lies between the chord AB and the arc AB

alt: Graph of y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1: the curve rises to a maximum at (1, 5), falls to a minimum at (3, 1) and then rises again; it crosses the y-axis at (0, 1).
caption: Figure: y = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 1 has a maximum at (1, 5) and a minimum at (3, 1)

alt: Graph of y = x^3 - 2x^2 + 1 with its tangent y = 4x - 7 touching the curve at P(2, 1), where the gradient 3x^2 - 4x equals 4.
caption: Figure: the tangent y = 4x − 7 touches the cubic at P(2, 1)

alt: Triangle with vertices A(1, 2), B(7, 4) and C(3, 9) drawn on a coordinate grid; the shoelace method gives its area as 19 square units.
caption: Figure: the triangle ABC whose area is found from its coordinates

alt: Graph of y = 3 sin 2x + 1 for 0 to 360 degrees: two complete waves of period 180 degrees about the centre line y = 1, with maxima of 4 at 45 and 225 degrees and minima of -2 at 135 and 315 degrees.
caption: Figure: y = 3 sin 2x + 1 has amplitude 3, period 180° and centre line y = 1

alt: Unit circle with the angle theta measured anticlockwise to the point (cos theta, sin theta) and the angle minus theta measured clockwise to (cos theta, minus sin theta): the two points have the same x-coordinate and opposite y-coordinates, so cos(-theta) = cos theta and sin(-theta) = -sin theta. Quadrants are labelled with the functions that are positive.
caption: Figure: the unit circle shows cos(−θ) = cos θ and sin(−θ) = −sin θ

alt: Vector AB from A(2, -1) to B(8, 7): 6 units across and 8 units up, so AB = 6i + 8j, and its length is the square root of 36 + 64, which is 10.
caption: Figure: the vector AB drawn with its components 6i and 8j

alt: Triangle OAB with OA = a and OB = b; N is the midpoint of OA and M the midpoint of AB, and the dashed line NM equals half of b, so NM is parallel to OB and half its length (the midpoint theorem).
caption: Figure: NM = ½b, so the line joining two midpoints is parallel to the third side

alt: Velocity-time graph of the kombi: it accelerates at 2 m/s^2 from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s, travels at 20 m/s until 70 s, then decelerates at 2.5 m/s^2 to rest at 78 s; the area under the graph, 1380 m, is the total distance.
caption: Figure: the area under the velocity-time graph is the distance travelled, 1380 m
